senses.gloss: An informal word for a strikingly attractive woman.
examples: She was cast as the blonde *bombshell* in the detective picture.
In the fifties the studio marketed her as a *bombshell*.
The part called for a *bombshell*, not the girl next door.

senses.gloss: A strip of paper, ribbon, or leather put between the pages of a book to mark your place.
examples: She slid a *bookmark* between the pages and set the novel down.
He uses old receipts as *bookmarks*.
The museum shop sells leather *bookmarks* stamped with its logo.

senses.gloss: A stage in a process that holds everything else up because it cannot go any faster.
examples: Legal review is the real *bottleneck* in our hiring.
One slow machine created a *bottleneck* on the whole assembly line.
They hired two more inspectors to clear the *bottleneck*.

senses.gloss: The burning of an owner's mark into the hide of cattle.
examples: *Branding* day brings every neighbor out to the ranch.
The calves are sorted and roped before the *branding* starts.
She learned to ride working spring *branding* in Montana.

senses.gloss: One of a trail of small clues or links left behind to show the way.
examples: The author drops *breadcrumbs* in chapter one that only make sense at the end.
Click the *breadcrumbs* at the top of the page to get back to the main category.
Investigators followed a *breadcrumb* trail of small cash payments.

senses.gloss: A failure that stops a vehicle or machine from working.
examples: We had a *breakdown* on the interstate and waited two hours for a tow.
The bus company reports a *breakdown* about once a month.
Regular service prevents most *breakdowns*.

senses.gloss: A division of something into its separate parts, usually with figures.
examples: Can you send me a *breakdown* of the costs by department?
The report includes a *breakdown* of voters by age.
She asked the shop for an itemized *breakdown* of the repair bill.

senses.gloss: A complete failure of something that had been working, such as talks, order, or a relationship.
examples: The strike followed a *breakdown* in negotiations.
There was a total *breakdown* of communication between the two offices.
A *breakdown* in law and order followed the storm.

senses.gloss: An escape from a prison or another guarded place.
examples: Three inmates planned the *breakout* for months.
The prison *breakout* made national news.
Guards stopped a *breakout* attempt last spring.

senses.gloss: The work or process of constructing something.
examples: The *building* of the new bridge took four years.
*Building* has slowed since interest rates went up.
The city halted all *building* near the shoreline.

senses.gloss: A short magazine or newsletter that an organization publishes regularly for its members.
examples: The wedding was announced in the church *bulletin*.
The club mails a *bulletin* to members every quarter.
I read about her prize in the alumni *bulletin*.

senses.gloss: A fast swimming stroke in which both arms sweep forward over the water together.
examples: She swims the *butterfly* in the two-hundred-meter final.
*Butterfly* is the hardest stroke to learn.
He shaved a second off his *butterfly* time this season.

senses.gloss: A fluttering feeling of nervousness in the stomach, usually used in the plural.
examples: I still get *butterflies* before a presentation.
She had *butterflies* the whole ride to the airport.
A few *butterflies* before a big game are perfectly normal.

senses.gloss: A cold weighing of one's own advantage.
examples: His apology was pure *calculation*, not regret.
The *calculation* was that voters would forget by November.
There was a certain *calculation* in the way she chose her friends.

senses.gloss: A system for dividing up the year that a country or religion follows.
examples: The Chinese *calendar* starts the new year in late January or February.
Most of the world now uses the Gregorian *calendar*.
Easter is set by a lunar *calendar*, so the date moves.

senses.gloss: A return phone call, especially one you are waiting for from an employer or a company.
examples: I interviewed on Tuesday and never got a *callback*.
Press one to request a *callback* instead of waiting on hold.
The insurer promised a *callback* within twenty-four hours.

senses.gloss: Cloth or clothing printed in a mottled green-and-brown pattern, worn by soldiers and hunters.
examples: He hunts in *camouflage* from head to toe.
Both boys wanted backpacks in *camouflage*.
Soldiers in desert *camouflage* were posted at the gate.

senses.gloss: A person or thing likely to get or to suffer something.
senses.ru: подходящий кандидат (на что-л.); тот, кому это грозит
examples: With that blood pressure, he's a prime *candidate* for a stroke.
The old warehouse is an obvious *candidate* for demolition.
Her knee makes her a good *candidate* for surgery.

senses.gloss: A jump into water with the knees pulled up to the chest to make a big splash.
examples: He did a *cannonball* off the diving board and soaked everyone.
No *cannonballs* in the shallow end!
Her *cannonball* sent a wave over the side of the pool.

senses.gloss: The official role or position in which someone is acting.
examples: She was there in her *capacity* as school board president.
I'm speaking in a private *capacity*, not for the company.
He signed the letter in his *capacity* as trustee.

senses.gloss: The ability to do or to understand something.
examples: Children have an amazing *capacity* for languages.
He no longer has the mental *capacity* to manage his own money.
She has an enormous *capacity* for hard work.

senses.gloss: A senior official of the Roman Catholic Church, ranking just below the pope.
examples: The *cardinals* met in Rome to elect a new pope.
He was made a *cardinal* at the age of fifty-eight.
The *cardinal* celebrated Mass at the cathedral downtown.
